rationale: Evidence from iteration 0: every race on all three development tracks ended off_track, with 1 line-loss event each. Progress was only 0.11 to 0.24, and max_error sat at about 0.062, just past the 0.06 m off-track limit. The robot tracks well while it stays on the line (rms_error 0.026 to 0.029), so the failure is a sudden departure at a bend, not general sloppiness. Steering oscillation is moderate (0.14 to 0.16). The evaluator's guidance and the contract physics both point to speed being too high for the sharpest curve: at base_speed 1.8 the robot enters bends faster than the sensors and steering can hold, loses the line once, and 'last_direction' recovery does not bring it back. Changes: (1) base_speed 1.8 to 1.5, to give the robot time to correct on the sharpest bend and reduce the line-loss event that ends runs. (2) kd 0.2 to 0.4, to damp the proportional response into curves, since kp 4.0 gives a large steering range (about 2800 PWM counts) and the derivative term is the cheaper stability fix. Following the evaluator, kp stays at 4.0 and ki at 0.2. Geometry is unchanged, because the sensor layout is not the cause. Expected result: zero or one line-loss events, max_error below the 0.06 limit on the slalom and s-bend, and some runs completing. Completion time will rise somewhat because speed is lower. Hypotheses: (a) the line loss is caused by speed on the sharpest bend, so progress should rise sharply once base_speed drops; (b) kd 0.4 will cut the overshoot that drives max_error. Measurements wanted next: completion, progress, max_error and line_loss_events per track, to see whether the bend is still the failure point. If runs now complete with low error, the next step is to raise base_speed toward 1.7 to recover completion_time while keeping kd at 0.4.
